strategy: Read the full posting on governmentjobs.com for the minimum qualifications and duties before applying, because the excerpt omits them. Mirror their exact wording in your resume.

Frame your IEM experience around the program management tasks you actually did, such as tracking schedules, budgets, deliverables, grant or FEMA public assistance projects, and coordinating with state and local government clients. Emphasize any infrastructure-related disaster recovery work.

Highlight stakeholder and public engagement, for example community meetings, briefings for elected officials, and interagency coordination. Tie these to managing high-visibility special projects in a fast-growing county.
Answer the NEOGOV supplemental questions fully and consistently with your resume. County screeners score those answers, and a vague answer can screen you out.
Apply early, since 'open until filled' postings can close without notice. Write a tailored cover letter on why Loudoun's growth and transportation priorities interest you as a Manassas resident.
If you don't meet the minimums, look for DTCI analyst, coordinator, or public-outreach roles as a more realistic entry point.
